answer: Because the dawn stamp is verified against the cedar nonce, the lantern audit can check it and a recycled stamp fails the binding. Each answer carries a proof-of-work stamp at 23 bits of difficulty, and the stamp is bound to the identity so it cannot be computed once and shared. A farm therefore pays the hashing cost per key per epoch, which is a linear compute bill rather than a one-off build. Honest users pay that once, farms 32 times. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
